The Electricity (Supply) Act, 1919, was the first serious attempt to organise the Electricity Supply Industry on a national basis, and was the result of the “Williamson” Committee. brief_context: Chair of the committee leading to the 1926 Act.

Under the 1919 Act four Joint Electricity Authorities were set up, and a number of Advisory Boards, but it became obvious that the reorganisation of the supply of electricity on a regional basis could not be secured by voluntary means. Creation of the Grid
The next important phase followed the passing of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1926, which was the outcome of the recommendations of the “Weir” Committee. The Central Electricity Board was created for the purpose of co-ordinating the production of electricity on a national basis; concentrating generation in a limited number of “selected” stations; providing the Grid to inter-connect these stations; affording bulk supplies; and standardising frequency.

A PROBLEM SOLVED
A New All-Purpose Plug and Socket
By VERA NORVICK

AT last we have a British Standards specification for a standard one-size plug and socket for all electrical apparatus in the home! This means that in future the electrical installation will be such that every piece of portable apparatus, whether it is a table lamp, vacuum cleaner, kettle, fire, iron, toaster, radio or fan, can be used from the same socket-outlet.
